docs.title: rn-forge-data
docs.text:
rn-forge-data holds Excel and tabular data helpers, built on rn-forge-commons.

The base install carries openpyxl and tablib[xlsx] and gives the Excel core, rn_forge.data. The pandas extra adds pandas for the adapter, rn_forge.data.pandas, which the core never imports.

Start with the guide, then the reference.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Notable changes to rn-forge-data, newest first, in the Keep a Changelog format.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Requires its rn-forge dependencies by version range from pykit's index (ADR-0004), not by git URL.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • The rn-forge-data package: Excel and tabular data helpers. The core, rn_forge.data, holds ExcelUtils, CellFormat, WorkbookTemplate and write_xlsx, and needs only openpyxl and tablib[xlsx]. The pandas adapter, rn_forge.data.pandas, behind the pandas extra, holds PandasUtils, ExcelAdapter, SeriesRow, series_value and series_columns. These moved from rn-forge-commons.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text: • Excel and pandas — workbooks, formats, write_xlsx, and the pandas adapter.

docs.title: Excel and pandas
docs.text: The package has one core and one adapter. rn_forge.data holds the Excel helpers, which need only openpyxl and tablib. rn_forge.data.pandas holds the pandas helpers and imports the core; the core never imports it, so importing rn_forge.data loads no pandas. The pandas extra installs pandas for the adapter, and the facade does not re-export the adapter.

docs.title: Workbooks
docs.text:
ExcelUtils creates, reads and writes openpyxl workbooks and formats rows. CellFormat carries the formatting to apply and WorkbookTemplate describes a sheet's columns and default formats.

from openpyxl.styles import Font
from rn_forge.data import CellFormat, ExcelUtils

workbook = ExcelUtils.new_workbook()
sheet = workbook.active
sheet.append(["id", "total"])
sheet.append([1001, 42.5])
ExcelUtils.format_row(sheet[2], CellFormat(font=Font(bold=True)))
ExcelUtils.write_workbook(workbook, "build/orders.xlsx")

ExcelUtils.FORMAT_CURRENCY, FORMAT_DATE and FORMAT_PERCENTAGE are ready made formats.

docs.title: Exporting a dataset
docs.text:
write_xlsx writes a tablib.Dataset to .xlsx bytes with a number format per column, which tablib's own xlsx writer does not offer. It streams through a write-only workbook, so large datasets stay cheap.

from datetime import date

import tablib
from rn_forge.data import write_xlsx

dataset = tablib.Dataset(headers=["name", "due", "total"])
dataset.append(["alice", date(2026, 1, 31), 42.5])
payload = write_xlsx(
    dataset, column_formats={"due": "yyyy-mm-dd", "total": "#,##0.00"}
)

A format for a name that is not a header raises KeyError.

docs.title: pandas
docs.text:
Use the adapter when the code wants pandas for transformation and openpyxl for workbook-level formatting. ExcelAdapter converts between workbooks and DataFrames, and PandasUtils reads typed fields from rows.

from rn_forge.data import ExcelUtils
from rn_forge.data.pandas import ExcelAdapter, PandasUtils

frames = ExcelAdapter.read_dataframe("orders.xlsx")
workbook = ExcelAdapter.from_dataframe(frames)
ExcelUtils.write_workbook(workbook, "build/orders-copy.xlsx")

row = frames["Sheet1"].iloc[0]
customer = PandasUtils.get_string_field(row, "customer_id")
total = PandasUtils.get_decimal_field(row, "total", precision=2)

series_value and series_columns give typed access to a row's value and labels, and SeriesRow is the row type.

docs.title: from_dict(data) classmethod
docs.text:
Create an instance from a dict, recursively rebuilding nested dataclasses.

Only keys that match declared dataclass field names are passed to the constructor. This makes from_dict tolerant of extra data (e.g. when loading from a config file that has fields added in a newer schema version). Nested dataclass-typed fields are reconstructed recursively for common container annotations, via :mod:dacite.

Note a nested dataclass field's own overridden from_dict (if any) is not called — dacite structures nested dataclasses itself.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data dict[str, Any]

A dict whose keys correspond to dataclass field names. Unrecognised keys are silently ignored, or rejected when the class's __dacite_config__ sets strict.

required

Returns:

Type Description Self

A new instance of this class populated with matching field values.

Raises:

Type Description AppException

A value does not match its field's declared type, a required field is absent, or an enum-typed field names a member the enum does not define. Under strict, also a key that names no field, at any nesting level; the message lists every such key by its dotted path (repository.archtype).

TypeError

If the subclass was not decorated with @dataclasses.dataclass.

docs.title: ExcelUtils
docs.text:
Excel workbook operations via openpyxl.

Requires openpyxl — install with rn-forge-data.

Typical workflow::

wb = ExcelUtils.new_workbook()
sheet = wb.active
sheet.title = "Orders"
sheet.append(["id", "total"])
sheet.append([1001, 42.50])
ExcelUtils.write_workbook(wb, "build/orders.xlsx")

The pandas adapter: row field extraction and Excel DataFrame conversion.

Requires the pandas extra.

docs.title: ExcelAdapter
docs.text:
Adapters between workbook primitives and pandas DataFrames.

Use this layer when the calling code wants pandas for transformation but openpyxl for workbook-level formatting or templating.

Example::

data = ExcelAdapter.read_dataframe("orders.xlsx")
workbook = ExcelAdapter.from_dataframe(data)
ExcelUtils.write_workbook(workbook, "build/orders-copy.xlsx")

docs.title: PandasUtils
docs.text:
Field extraction from pandas DataFrame and Series rows.

Requires pandas — install with rn-forge-data[pandas].

Example::

row = df.iloc[0]
customer_id = PandasUtils.get_string_field(row, "customer_id")
total = PandasUtils.get_decimal_field(row, "total", precision=2)

docs.title: series_value(row, field_name)

Return row[field_name], normalized to Any.

Series.__getitem__ has a wide overload set; pinning the result to Any here keeps the variation out of every call site.
